definitions.explanation: What really exists or happens, as opposed to theory or imagination.
Used adverbially to emphasize the truth or reality of something.

examples.japanese: {実際|じっさい}に{見|み}てみないと{分|わ}からない。
examples.english: You won't understand unless you actually see it.

examples.japanese: {実際|じっさい}は{違|ちが}うんです。
{理論|りろん}と{実際|じっさい}は{違|ちが}う。
{実際|じっさい}の{生活|せいかつ}はもっと{大変|たいへん}だ。
{実際|じっさい}に{行|い}ってみたら、{思|おも}ったより{静|しず}かだった。
examples.english: When I actually went there, it was quieter than I expected.

examples.japanese: {写真|しゃしん}で{見|み}るのと{実際|じっさい}に{見|み}るのとでは、{全然|ぜんぜん}{印象|いんしょう}が{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: Seeing something in photos versus seeing it in reality gives a completely different impression.

notes:
Functions as both a noun and an adverb.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{実際|じっさい}に (actually, in reality)
・{実際|じっさい}は (in fact, actually)
・{実際|じっさい}の + noun ({実際|じっさい}の{問題|もんだい} = actual problem)
・{実際|じっさい}に{会|あ}う (meet in person)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{実|じつ}は - actually, to tell the truth (more confession-like)
・{本当|ほんとう}は - really, in truth
・{現実|げんじつ} - reality (noun only)
